claims.text: Adversarial debiasing on the UCI Adult Dataset reduced predictive accuracy slightly from 86.0% to 84.5%.
On the UCI Adult Dataset with adversarial debiasing, false negative rates across female (0.0647) and male (0.0701) subgroups showed no statistically significant difference (p = 0.62).
On the UCI Adult Dataset with adversarial debiasing, false positive rates across female (0.4458) and male (0.4349) subgroups showed no statistically significant difference (p = 0.25).
In word analogy task debiasing, the dot product between the learned parameter vector w and the gender direction g increased from 0.08 without debiasing to 0.55 with debiasing.
Removing a protected variable directly from training data fails to yield a debiased model because other features remain correlated with the protected variable.

evidence.description: The authors state that debiasing has only a small effect on overall accuracy (86.0% vs 84.5%) on the UCI Adult dataset.
With debiasing, FNR values are 0.0647 for females and 0.0701 for males, with a two-proportion two-tail large sample z-test yielding p = 0.62.
With debiasing, FPR values are 0.4458 for females and 0.4349 for males, with a two-proportion two-tail large sample z-test yielding p = 0.25.
Without debiasing, w^T g = 0.08 and ||w|| = 0.82; with debiasing, w^T g = 0.55 and ||w|| = 0.96.
Citing Lum and Johndrow (2016), the paper notes that removing protected variables fails to debias due to variable correlations.

methodologies.name: Adversarial Debiasing Framework
methodologies.description: Simultaneously trains a predictor network to predict target Y and an adversary network predicting protected variable Z, modifying predictor weight updates via gradient projection and hyperparameter scaling to minimize protected variable information.

limitations.text: Removing the protected variable from training data fails to eliminate bias because other variables remain correlated with it.
The adversarial training algorithm can run into local minima and produce results closer to demographic parity than equality of odds unless hyperparameter scaling is carefully adjusted over time.
Theoretical convergence guarantees rely on assumptions of loss function concavity and convexity that are generally not satisfied in standard neural network architectures.

future_work.text: Investigate whether debiased word embeddings maintain utility in downstream tasks beyond simple word analogies.
Develop training stabilization techniques to prevent algorithmic divergence when hyperparameters are improperly tuned.
Explore combining multiple adversaries to eliminate demographic and racial biases in image recognition systems.
Determine whether complex predictors require correspondingly complex adversaries in continuous protected/target variable scenarios.
